fixed.how: edge-bff now uses one rule, terminal_access.relayed (apps/edge-bff/app/terminal_access.py:303), for every terminal-api answer it relays: forward_terminal, relay_cut and PageFiles all go through it. A terminal-api 401, any 403 other than capability_required, a 400 about edge-bff's own owner headers, and every 5xx become 503 TERMINAL_UNAVAILABLE in the contract shape, logged as terminal_refused with the upstream status and code. A 429 becomes 429 LIMIT_REACHED with details.limit terminal.<quota>, allowed, retry_after_s and the Retry-After header. A 400 about the request is answered 400 INVALID_INPUT, and a 404 is answered 404 NOT_FOUND; both carry terminal-api's code as details.reason. capability_required becomes CAPABILITY_REQUIRED with its display name. terminal-api's message text never reaches the page. On terminal-api, take() now raises quota_exceeded with quota, limit, window and retry_after_s, and sets the Retry-After header (wait_error). The wait comes from Store.frees_in: the seconds until the rolling window lets the refused request fit, read only on a refusal and never longer than the window. The service ceiling and the sign-in throttle send Retry-After too. In the Terminal page, live.ts now shows the contract's words instead of the code. fixed.how: The switch-off session read (store.session) now accepts only sessions with no account (user_id IS NULL), which is what the switch-off sign-in writes. So a switch-on session that has not passed MFA, is idle, or belongs to a disabled user no longer becomes a '*' session on a switch-off site. With the decided pairing (beta off, live on) this also ties every session to the site that made it, with no sessions.site column.

Migration 20261119_022 adds identities.seed_verifier_sha256 (the sha256 of the verifier the seed last wrote, never the verifier itself) and fills it for the seed's own identity. AccountStore.seed copies EDGE_PASSWORD_VERIFIER only while sha256(verifier) still equals that mark. After a password change or reset on the switch-on site the identity belongs to the account and is never overwritten (logged account_seed_password_kept). The switch-off sign-in still reads the environment value directly. The recorded rule changed, so the README switch table and the seed docstring were updated.

fixed.how: Migrations 20261119_020 and _021 add site (NOT NULL DEFAULT 'beta', CHECK beta|live) to edge_bff.jobs and edge_bff.backtest_jobs. Store.submit, Store.claim and _promote carry and filter the site. BacktestStore(store, site) claims, reaps and prunes only its own site's jobs. The AI worker's claim is bound to the app's site (worker.claim, the same pattern as worker.access). Per-loop switches replace the single all-or-nothing switch: EDGE_AI_WORKER_ENABLED (unset means beta only; true on live is refused), EDGE_BACKTEST_LOOP_ENABLED, EDGE_HOUSEKEEPING_ENABLED, and EDGE_EMAIL_ENABLED (the sender runs only with the switch on, so only on live). EDGE_WORKER_ENABLED=false still turns every loop off.

Duplicate of R2-7 plus R2-2, closed by the same fixes. config.validate also refuses the mixed pairings: EDGE_SITE=live without EDGE_MULTIUSER, and the beta with EDGE_MULTIUSER on outside EDGE_ENVIRONMENT=local.

Duplicate of R2-7. The email outbox needs no site column: only the switch-on site (live) writes it and runs the sender. The hourly housekeeping runs in its own task, and an advisory try-lock on each purge stops two sites running the same purge at once.

Parts 1 and 2 are fixed as R2-7 and R2-2. EDGE_SITE (beta|live, default beta) is in place, and the live site masks every principal: principal.beta_only, live_view and Auth.site_view. On live nothing in the Monitor or admin tabs, no admin right from rights.py and no lab item is ever held, '*' included ('*' reads as every catalog flag that is not beta-only). allow_of never sends '*' from live. Auth.need answers 404 NOT_FOUND for those capabilities before the session is read, and /monitor and /c/<id> answer 404 too. MFA is still decided by the account's own grants, so user #1 needs MFA on live. Part 3 (the expand-then-contract order for 20261118_001 and 3c step 4) needs no code and is written into the notes for the records track. The pending test moved into apps/edge-bff/tests/ and was changed to the decided pairing (see notes).

What can be checked from one process: config.shared_key_marks() writes a 12-hex HMAC mark of EDGE_SESSION_SECRET, EDGE_CODE_SECRET and EDGE_MFA_KEY into every startup_done log line. The two services' lines then show whether they hold the same values, without logging any secret. The rule itself (edge-bff-live takes all three as ${{edge-bff.NAME}} references) is in the railway.ts comment block and in the notes for CONTRACT 16.

The secrets part is handled as in R2-8. The log-mode guard no longer accepts EDGE_ENVIRONMENT=dev, which is also the live site's Railway environment. Log mode with the switch on now needs EDGE_ENVIRONMENT=local or an explicit EDGE_EMAIL_LOG_ALLOWED=true. That flag exists for a deliberate test on the live site before the Resend key, with no real person (the user asked on 2026-11-19 to test directly on weblive). While it is on, email_log_mode_allowed is logged at every start.

The start-up now runs as one attempt under a lock: readiness, seed, catalog names, seed plan, then the loops. The attempt runs in the lifespan, is retried every EDGE_POLL_SECONDS and on each /ready, and /ready answers 503 until it succeeds. No loop starts before that, the backtest loop included (store.ready reads no backtest table, so the reason for the old comment still holds). With the switch on, a failing seed fails the attempt. New log lines: startup_not_ready and startup_done.

The same start-up fix as R2-3. EDGE_WORKER_ENABLED, EDGE_EMAIL_ENABLED and the new loop switches are parsed with switch_of, so a typo stops the start. email_sender_off is logged at error level whenever the switch is on and no sender runs.

The purges left the AI loop for worker.Housekeeping, a task of their own that also runs on live, where there is no AI loop. Each purge in store.PURGES (sessions, throttle, pending) now has its own transaction and its own try. It deletes at most 500 rows per batch (by key) and at most 20 batches per turn. A failed purge is retried after a backoff that doubles up to an hour, is logged as housekeeping_failed by error class, and is skipped while another instance holds its try-lock. purge_pending and throttle.purge take an optional limit and return the row count. BacktestLoop.run now runs prune (by site, batched), reap and claim each in its own try, and a failed prune backs off.

decisions_needed.context: Every email EDGE sends leaves a row in the database's email outbox: the recipient's address, the kind of email (a code, 'password changed', 'account exists'), when it was sent and Resend's id. The email's text is removed once it is sent. Until now nothing ever deleted these rows. This branch deletes them 24 h after they were made, but only for addresses that have no EDGE account (registrations that were never verified, which CONTRACT 4 already deletes after 24 h, or addresses never registered). Rows of addresses that do have an account are kept for ever. With accounts switched on, each account adds a row for every code, reset and password change (up to 10 a day). EDGE reads only the last 24 h (the 60-second and daily limits), and Resend's idempotency key lasts 24 h, so nothing needs an older row. Used email codes and Resend webhook events also pile up. The Phase 6 Privacy text must state a retention period.
decisions_needed.options: A: delete sent, failed, expired and suppressed rows of every address after 30 days, and the same for used codes and webhook events. B: delete after 24 h. C: keep them while the account exists and delete them with it. D: another period you name.
decisions_needed.recommendation: A. It is one migration that replaces edge_bff.purge_email_outbox().

decisions_needed.context: Sign-in to the beta website (accounts switched off, admin only, login EDGE_LOGIN) is now limited per login and per client address: 10 wrong passwords per 15 minutes from one address. A stranger can no longer keep the admin out just by typing the login. The new per-account cap (at most 100 wrong passwords in a row, the NIST SP 800-63B-4 rule) is built only with accounts switched on, where 'Forgot password?' is the way back. The beta has no reset. If the cap applied there, anyone who sent 100 wrong passwords would lock the admin out for 24 h, again and again, and only the operator script could unlock it. Without the cap, someone with many client addresses can guess the beta admin's password at up to about 960 tries a day per address, and the beta has no second sign-in step with accounts off.
decisions_needed.options: A: no cap on the beta (as built), with a long random admin password. B: the same 100-cap with its 24 h lock on the beta; the way back is scripts/edge_mfa_unlock.py or waiting. C: open the beta website only to known client addresses (a Railway change).
decisions_needed.recommendation: A now. Add C if the beta's address becomes widely known.

decisions_needed.context: 'Forgot password?' emails a new 6-digit code, and each new code cancels the one before (CONTRACT 1). An address gets at most 10 EDGE emails a day. Anyone who knows an account's email address can press 'Forgot password?' for it. Every minute that cancels the owner's code (the owner gets the new code too, so this alone is a nuisance). After 10 presses in a day, the owner's own 'Forgot password?' sends nothing until the next day. This branch stopped notification emails from holding codes back (R2-10) and limited registrations by others (R1-13), but this budget is still shared by design.
decisions_needed.options: A: keep as is. The owner may wait up to a day after such an attack, but the sign-in limit and the account cap no longer lock them out. B: a 'Forgot password?' within a live code's 5 minutes sends nothing and keeps that code (fewer emails; someone who lost the email waits 5 minutes). C: count resets per address and client address, so a stranger's presses do not use the owner's budget (but then many client addresses could flood one mailbox).

decisions_needed.context: An admin who changes phone sets up a new authenticator from a session that has already passed the second sign-in step. This branch keeps the old authenticator working until the new one is proved by its first code, so a password alone can no longer take over the second step (R1-7). But someone who steals an admin's already-verified session cookie can still start and confirm an authenticator of their own, because starting one asks for no fresh code. OWASP's MFA cheat sheet asks for the current factor before it is changed.
decisions_needed.options: A: the request that starts a new authenticator must carry a code from the current one (or a recovery code); the set-up screen gets a code field. B: the session must have passed the second step in the last 10 minutes, otherwise it verifies again first. C: keep as built.
decisions_needed.recommendation: B. No page change, and it fits the re-check's own test, which starts a re-enrolment right after MFA.

decisions_needed.context: Passwords are stored as scrypt verifiers. Following the fix round's brief (R2-29), this branch raises the cost from N=2^14, r=8, p=1 to OWASP's minimum equivalent at 16 MiB, N=2^14, r=8, p=5. Measured on this machine: 52 ms per derivation at p=1, 235 ms at p=5. A sign-in with accounts switched on (the live website) derives 4 times (one for the account and 3 padding, so the time reveals nothing), which is about 0.9 s of CPU per sign-in. At most 4 derivations run at once on the new password pool, so a burst of sign-ins waits its turn. Old verifiers keep working and are replaced at each account's next sign-in. The edge-bff test suite took about 19 min instead of 12.5 min on this shared machine.
decisions_needed.options: A: keep p=5 (as built). B: N=2^15, r=8, p=3 (32 MiB, about the same CPU). C: go back to p=1 and record it as accepted in CONTRACT 4 (5 times weaker against a database leak).
